newsitem.title: DUBAI: Explosion rocks Bahrain hotel, no casualty reports.
newsitem.headline: Explosion rocks Bahrain hotel, no casualty reports.

text.p: An explosion rocked a hotel in central Manama early on Tuesday, smashing a hotel window but not causing any injuries, an executive of the hotel said.
"It was a simple, small explosion outside the hotel," the executive at the four-star Delmon Hotel told Reuters by telephone from Manama.
"One window was broken. I think it was a bomb. No one was hurt, everyone is safe," he said, adding the blast occured at around 4.15 a.m. (0115 GMT) this morning.
A government spokesman said initial reports showed the explosion appeared to have been caused by a gas leak. He added there was no indication that the blast was caused by an attack.
"We have no injuries, and the investigation is still going on," he said.
Witnesses said part of the roof of the hotel's nightclub had collapsed due to the explosion. They said workers were clearing up the area and police were setting up checkpoints nearby.
More than two dozen people have been killed in over two years of anti-government protests in the Gulf Arab state. Hundreds of people have been arrested.

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to press the Sunni-led government to implement economic and political reforms.
A series of arson attacks in early June were described by a government official as "continued acts of terrorism".
